source.title: Symmetry without a manifold: intrinsic dimension on orbits
source.authors: Chon-Fai Kam; M. Bessafi; Frédéric Cadet

record.tranche_reason: The study measures loss scaling on modular addition and reports systematic departures from a power law, alongside dependence of fitted rates on fitting choices, training setup, and data supply. It is a challenge/refinement in a different task regime, not a reproduction of language-model scaling experiments.
record.gate_note: The study tests scaling behavior on modular-addition networks, not language-model pretraining. It reports no small-run-to-large-run extrapolation test, compute-optimal parameter/token allocation, fixed-parameter architecture-shape comparison, or downstream-task prediction. Intrinsic-dimension and spectral-occupancy results are not rows because they do not measure a versioned scaling behavior. The critical-width result is recorded as a related finding outside the listed versions.
record.test_reason: Two-layer networks on modular addition, with held-out loss swept over width (N = 3ph). A floor power law is rejected at every group order, with ΔAIC 25.5–40.9 and arc-shaped residuals, in favour of a floor exponential. The power-law exponent moves with group order, and the fitted rate depends on fitting and setup choices. This argues that the power-law form (V5) fails in this regime and bears on V7. It is not a language-model reproduction.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right but incomplete. The authors conclude that the modular-addition test loss is a floor exponential in width, not a power law, and that with sufficient data the rate factorises: weight decay sets it, not group order. The same holds at every fixed α, with departures at p = 23 and under ReLU that they attribute to data supply. They also argue that intrinsic dimension is undefined on group-orbit representations, so the geometric 4/d derivation has no input. Finally, they find that critical width falls with group order, against capacity counting.
record.recipe_differences: The study trains two-layer networks on modular addition rather than language models on text; it sweeps hidden width and weight decay, not pretraining tokens or compute, and compares exponential and power-law fits.
record.method_sensitivity: Fitted rate changes with weight decay and fixed exponent α; group-order dependence differs under ReLU and at p = 23, and changes when the training fraction is raised. Width truncation matters when the exponential floor is not resolved.

fits_no_version.finding: Critical width for 0.9 held-out accuracy falls from 34.1 at p = 23 to 26.6 at p = 113.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In modular addition, the width needed to generalise falls as group order grows.

fits_no_version.finding: Within the quadratic, data-sufficient regime, the exponential rate is set by weight decay and is nearly independent of group order (1.097x spread, below seed resolution).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In algebraic tasks, the loss-decay rate with width belongs to the regulariser rather than to task size.

record.problems: The exponent α is not identified over the available width range; the authors report that rates vary by a factor of 214 as fixed α varies from 0.75 to 2 while fit quality changes little. Several large-width loss floors are affected by plateau noise. The factorisation is below the experiment’s resolution for p ≥ 47, and the p = 23 and ReLU results show qualifications related to data supply.
record.rows_left_out: No rows omitted for the tested scaling results. Intrinsic-dimension, simplex, and spectral-occupancy measurements are not extracted as scaling-law rows; they do not directly measure a listed version. The text also reports other diagnostics of fit validity and critical-width comparisons, but only the version-relevant outcomes and the distinct critical-width finding are tabulated.

untested.parts: All of it: no language-model pretraining loss.
All of it: no extrapolation from small to large runs.
All of it: no fixed-compute allocation of parameters vs tokens.
All of it: no depth/width comparison at fixed parameter count.
Only width (parameter) scaling on modular addition is tested. Not tested: data or compute scaling axes, image/video, repeated data, fine-tuning, transfer.
All of it: no downstream-task prediction.
Not tested: compute-optimal split, parameter-counting conventions, training schedule, and disagreement between published LM laws.

missing.what: Truncation sensitivity of the fitted parameter. Plain exponential drifts up to 105%; floor exponential drifts 0.3%; matched power law drifts 12–30% on dropping the largest widths.
missing.locator: Section 3; Table 8 drift column; Appendix E.6

missing.what: Power-law rejection holds at every fixed α 0.75–2; smallest ΔAIC is 18.8 at α = 0.75.
Learning-rate change barely moves the quadratic rate: c(1e-2)/c(3e-3) = 0.98 ± 0.04.
Floor L∞ vs Kmax log-log slope −4.5 up to Kmax = 26, flattening to −1.1 where plateau noise dominates.

record.verdict_notes: This is a toy setting (two-layer MLP on modular addition, width up to 128, under one decade of usable width). It bears on V5 and V7 only by analogy to the language-model claim. The rows linked to V7 for rate dependence concern the rate of an exponential, not power-law exponents. The paper's main claim is in fact that one setup variable (group order) does not move that rate. Rows r10–r27 are individual Table 6 cells and should be merged into r28 or kept as supporting data. Neither original source is this study.

versions.untested_parts: The study does not test held-out pretraining loss of language models.
No prediction of much larger runs from fits to small runs.
No fixed-compute sweep or loss-minimising parameter/token allocation.
No comparison of depth, width, or other architecture details at fixed parameter count.
Tests modular-addition training, including quadratic and ReLU activations; does not test image/video modalities, repeated data, fine-tuning, transfer, or other listed regimes.
No downstream-task performance prediction from scale or pretraining loss.
Tests fit- and setup-dependence for modular-addition loss curves, but not disagreement between the original sources’ compute-optimal allocation laws.

relation.reason: The study measures held-out loss across widths and compares functional forms; its own results test V5 and V7.

tranche.reason: The matched fits and residual tests reject power-law loss scaling in this non-text training regime, directly challenging V5.

source_check.notes: The authors leave exponential exponent α unidentified. The matched exponential also has significant residual structure at three of eight group orders; its superior fit does not establish a uniquely determined functional form.
